notice: A ceiling is the highest level this evidence could support. It is not a verified level: a SLSA Build level needs an assessment of the build platform, and an ALPS level needs an independent verifier.

slsa_build.basis: signed by a keyless workflow identity on a runner not observed to be provider-hosted; a higher level depends on whether you treat your runner operator as the build platform

alps.basis: signed by a CI workflow identity; platform issuance is not assessed yet, so ALPS-1 is not reported

next_steps.why: SLSA Build L2 needs a hosted build platform. A laptop is never one. On a self-hosted runner, CircleCI or Kubernetes it depends on whether you treat your runner operator as the build platform; a provider-hosted runner (GitHub-hosted, gitlab.com SaaS, Buildkite hosted) removes that question.
next_steps.action: Move this build into a CI job on a provider-hosted runner, for example a GitHub Actions job with `runs-on: ubuntu-latest`. On a self-hosted runner, tell your human that this level depends on whether they treat the runner operator as the build platform.

next_steps.why: Inline provenance is signed by the same workflow identity the build steps can mint, so a build step can forge it (issue #9822). L3 needs a separate builder identity, which only GitHub Actions' reusable-workflow identity provides.
next_steps.action: Coming, not yet published: the isolated provenance workflow aflock-ai/cilock-action/.github/workflows/provenance.yml. Do not add it yet; re-run cilock after it ships for the pinned snippet.

next_steps.why: ALPS 2 needs an enforced sandbox and a non-agent observer that signs the boundary. cilock records no boundary today, so no run can present ALPS 2 evidence yet.
next_steps.action: Coming, not yet available: boundary attestation. You cannot sandbox yourself; ask your human to launch you inside the recommended sandbox (https://pushgate.dev/docs/agent-sandbox) so your runs already have the boundary the attestation will record.
